content: The test image shows a corn plant with prominent yellow-white and green alternating parallel stripes along the entire length of the leaves, with some leaves appearing shredded/disintegrated. The reference Downy Mildew images show early-stage plants, but the symptom description is a strong match: "white parallel stripes of varying width alternating with green tissue; the white-striped areas eventually turn brown and disintegrate, resulting in a shredded appearance."

**Key observations from the test image:**
- Broad white/yellow stripes alternating with green tissue running parallel along the full leaf length
- White-striped areas showing disintegration/shredded texture
- Plant appears somewhat stunted
- Classic "striped" appearance from base to tip

This matches Downy Mildew very precisely. Maize Streak Virus would produce narrow streaks, not these broad white bands. The shredded/disintegrating appearance of the pale tissue is the hallmark of Downy Mildew.
